title: Catalog Undo can remain behind a continuously open Android keyboard
severity_source: Agent triage: recovery is inaccessible until the keyboard is hidden, while its expiry timer continues.
source: Native regression validation for UI-036; independently reproduced on the original APK without pressing Clear.
environment: Qt 6.12.0, isolated API-36 x86_64 emulator, English Gboard; no physical-phone reproduction claimed.
reproduction: Use disposable data: the emulator fixture has default and weekly lists. On a phone, create an unused temporary list; never delete a real list for this test.
Open the drawer, select Light theme, select Lists in the list selector, and close the drawer. The visible rows must be list names, not items inside a shopping list.
Double-tap the temporary list row. Its unchanged name must appear in the movable editor with Gboard open; tap the text field only if needed to open Gboard now.
Press the native Gboard Return key without changing the name. Confirm the named row returns and Gboard remains open.
From this point do not press Clear, Back, open the drawer, or tap the editor to reopen Gboard. If Gboard closes, the continuously-open-IME precondition was not met.
While Gboard is still open, swipe the temporary list row RIGHT far enough to activate deletion. Release and inspect Undo immediately, before its 15-second countdown expires.

Expected: Undo is visible and tappable above Gboard. Emulator failure: no Undo above Gboard. In the failing case, hide Gboard with one Back promptly; Undo then appears at the bottom. Tap it to restore the list before expiry.
actual: Undo is absent above the visible IME. Hiding Gboard reveals it at y=2788..2991; it was behind the keyboard rather than already expired.
expected: Undo stays visible and tappable above the native IME while its timer runs, and restores the exact catalog identities/order and contents.
evidence: Original-APK comparison: out/ui036/catalog-original-no-clear-probe/probe.json and screenshots. Clear/reopen on the original APK instead places Undo at y=1696..1899, above IME top 1944. Retaining focus in UI-036 exposes the continuous-IME path too.
source_review: Read-only instrumentation found the Qt window/View stayed full height while the native IME was visible. The platform resize/inset cause is not established. Temporary instrumentation and unsuccessful focus/commit/show experiments were removed; do not add guessed keyboard padding or change Theme density.
regression: tests/android/test_entry.py --catalog-ime-only retains the no-Clear trigger and catalog_undo_reachable_above_ime assertion. The full entry driver checks the same visible target after rename/delete. This is an explicit failing reproduction, not an XFAIL or a passing acceptance test.
scope: Backlog only. UI-036 fixes Clear focus; this separate native layout bug remains open. A fix needs failing-before/passing-after native coverage, normal keyboard hide/reopen and reachable Undo checks.
verification_before: Original APK: tests/android/test_entry.py --catalog-ime-only passes catalog_accept_preserves_rows_and_ime and fails catalog_undo_reachable_above_ime. Exact observations and frames: out/ui036/android-catalog-before. The precondition uses canonical UUIDs and compares saved rows exactly.
verification_current: Final UI-036 APK repeats the same no-Clear failure: precondition passes, catalog_undo_reachable_above_ime fails (out/ui036/android-catalog-final/results.json). UI-037 remains open; no native broad-pass claim.
phone_report: 2026-11-19: user tried the ticket steps but could not reproduce on Android, then requested more precise steps. Expanded catalog/Return/continuous-IME/direction/timing instructions supplied; exact phone retest pending. Known failing scope remains the tested API-36 emulator configuration.
classification: Confirmed rendered symptom on the API-36 emulator, reproduced on original and fixed APKs. Application-versus-Qt/platform/test-environment cause remains unconfirmed. Keep open for platform investigation; no layout workaround selected.
proposed_margin_review: Windows already reserves DevelopmentKeyboard.occupiedHeight in View.bottomPadding. ListView.bottomMargin provides scrollable room but does not move the viewport-anchored UndoBar. Android normally uses native window resizing; adding the entire keyboard height without measuring actual overlap risks double reservation. No geometry change made.
